newsitem.title: USA: CBS announces Molinari to join network.
newsitem.headline: CBS announces Molinari to join network.

text.p: Rep. Susan Molinari of New York, a senior Republican in the House of Representatives, will leave Congress and become a co-anchor on a new CBS Saturday morning news program, CBS said on Wednesday.
Molinari, who represents Staten Island, New York, will vacate her seat in July, the announcement said.
In a statement faxed to Reuters, CBS said Molinari would be "a co-anchor of CBS New Saturday Morning, a new program to be broadcast Saturdays...beginning this fall."

It quoted Andrew Heyward, President, CBS News, as saying Molinari was "a smart, compelling communicator who also happens to be a working mom interested in many of the same issues our audience is interested in."

Molinari, 39, said in the statement she was grateful for the people of her district for giving her the chance to serve them for the last seven years and added: "I loved and continue to love that job, but this unique -- and unexpected -- opportunity with CBS News is one I became more and more intrigued with and ultimately decided I couldn't pass up."

Molinari was the keynote speaker at the 1996 Republican National Convention in San Diego and is considered one of the party's leading women politicians. Westinghouse Electric Corp is the parent company of CBS News.
